title: Bad Bunny Wraps Record-Breaking $467 Million World Tour: By the Numbers
summary: The DTMF World Tour drew to a close after shows on five continents.
contentText:
On Wednesday (July 22), Bad Bunny played the final show of the Debí Tirar Más Fotos World Tour. According to figures reported to Billboard Boxscore, it grossed $467.5 million and sold 3.1 million tickets over 55 shows, setting several records in the process.

The DTMF World tour follows Debí Tirar Más Fotos , released in January 2025. That sent went on to top the Billboard 200 for five weeks, spread between January, February, and May of 2025, plus a return in February 2026. It birthed his first solo No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 (“DtMF”), two more top five hits, and another 14 chart entries, ultimately placing all 17 of the album’s tracks on the Hot 100.

Debí Tirar Más Fotos was further supported by a 13-minute narrative film, several individual music videos, a Tiny Desk Concert for NPR, hosting the season premier of Saturday Night Live , getting announced as the Super Bowl Halftime performer, six Grammy nominations, and a 31-show hometown residency Jose Miguel Agrelot Coliseum in San Juan, Puerto Rico – all before heading out on the album’s proper tour.

The DTMF World Tour kicked off on November 21 at Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic with the first of 55 performances. But it wasn’t merely an isolated victory lap after the album cycle: in back-to-back weekends at the beginning of the new year, Debí Tirar Más Fotos won album of the year at the 68th Annual Grammy Awards and his Super Bowl set made eye-popping chart impact, bringing Bad Bunny back to the top of the Billboard 200 and Hot 100, more than a year after the album’s release.

Amidst it all, the DTMF World Tour broke international Boxscore records and properly concluded this epic album cycle. Scroll below for a full breakdown of the tour’s successes, by the numbers.
